newsitem.title: MEXICO: Telmex says confident will avoid strike.
newsitem.headline: Telmex says confident will avoid strike.

text.p: Mexican telephone giant Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) said on Monday it was confident it would reach an agreement on a proposed wage hike with its workers and stave off a potential strike.
"Talks are only just beginning...we have until the third week in April," Gerardo Munoz, head of investor relations, told Reuters.

"(But) we have a very strong, solid relationship with the union. In general terms, both sides have always shown a willingness to negotiate and compromise and there is no reason for that to change now," Munoz added in a telephone interview.

Telmex's 50,000 strong union last week asked the telephone giant for a 47.43 percent wage hike for this year. The union said it would call a strike for April 25 if it was unsatisfied with the company's counter-offer.

Telmex workers won a 27 percent wage hike in 1996, but workers have complained that wages have fallen behind inflation, which was about 28 percent last year and 52 percent in 1995. Consumer prices are expected to rise some 17 percent this year.
